clue.text: Girl formerly without love gets boy

parts.note: Clare is a girl's name

indicators.note: without tells us a letter is dropped from the word for formerly

parts.note: once means formerly, at an earlier time
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: An ex-girlfriend gone cold on romance takes up with a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formerly' looks like part of a girl's past, but it is ONCE; 'without' drops the O, which is love as a tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarence is a male given name, so it names a boy.

clue.text: Teases guys very loudly rather than quietly

indicators.note: rather than says one letter stands in place of another in the word for guys

parts.note: chaps are guys, men
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loudly

explanation.surface: Blokes tease each other by shouting instead of speaking softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather than' replaces P in CHAPS with FF.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff is to banter or tease good-humouredly.

clue.text: Gold volume discovered in grave

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a stere is a cubic metre, a unit of volume

explanation.surface: A hoard of gold is unearthed in a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' is the adjective meaning serious, not a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and grave both mean stern and serious in manner.

clue.text: Praising European institution with reason: German is included

parts.note: the EU is the European Union

indicators.note: included says the German word goes inside the word for reason

parts.note: logic is reasoning
ist is German for is

explanation.surface: A tribute to an EU body for its rationality, with Germany taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' acts on the German word: IST sits inside LOGIC, not after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eulogistic means full of praise, like a eulogy.

clue.text: I am thinking? So I am — in Latin!

definitions.text: I am thinking? So I am — in Latin!

parts.words: I am thinking? So I am — in Latin!
parts.note: a jokey rendering of Descartes's famous principle, asking for its original Latin wording

explanation.definitionFit: Descartes's Latin dictum translates as I think, therefore I am.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation has parking about? Terrific!

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
re means about or concerning, as in business letters
fab, short for fabulous, means terrific

explanation.surface: An estate agent enthuses that a temporary home comes with parking nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: A prefab is a prefabricated house, of the kind built in Britain as stopgap housing after the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated house was put up quickly as a short-term dwelling, hence temporary housing.

clue.text: Part of film has proper sound

indicators.note: sound means the word is said aloud

parts.note: real means proper, genuine

explanation.surface: A section of a movie has decent audio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' signals that REAL is heard as its homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool of film, one section of a feature.

clue.text: Fussy tot poked into plate

indicators.note: poked into means pushed inside the word for plate

parts.note: a fish is a flat plate of wood or iron used to strengthen a joint, as in a fishplate on railway track
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A picky toddler jabs at food on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler but is the verb tot up, to add; a fish is also a strengthening plate, as in a railway fishplate.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddish means given to fads, so fussy about particular things such as food.

clue.text: Pub has appeal to individual singer

parts.note: a bar is a pub
it means sex appeal, as in the 1920s 'It girl'
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A pub stages a charity appeal for a solo vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer with a voice between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Animal needing help? Not half!

indicators.note: not half, an exclamation meaning very much, here literally means only half of the word for help is kept

explanation.surface: A creature in trouble is asked if it wants assistance and roars 'Not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'Absolutely!', but here it means take only half of ASSIST (help).
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a donkey, a familiar beast of burden.

clue.text: Support a learner and offer money

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
to tender is to offer, as in tendering a bid

explanation.surface: Someone helps a novice along and offers to pay cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is currency that must by law be accepted as payment, so it is money.

clue.text: Soldiers land on railway, enthralling little child

parts.note: to light is to land or alight, as a bird does
an infant is a little child

explanation.surface: Troops arrive on a train line, which captivates a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: To light is to alight or land; in this down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Light infantry are lightly equipped foot soldiers.

clue.text: Conveyance of goods has number and period recorded by father

indicators.note: recorded by means written down after the word for father, so father goes first

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
eight is a number
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dad logs a shipment's figure and its date in the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorded by' tells us father is written first, before the number and period.
explanation.definitionFit: Freightage is the carrying of freight, which means transporting goods.

clue.text: Tantrum when receiving a decree

indicators.note: receiving means the word for tantrum takes the letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: a fit of temper is a tantrum

explanation.surface: Someone throws a tantrum when an order is handed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts A inside FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative order, so it means a decree.

clue.text: Foreign gentlemen dance about at first with erotic desire

indicators.note: at first means the word for about comes in front of the word for dance

parts.note: ca. (circa) means about
a ball is a formal dance
eros is erotic love or desire

explanation.surface: Gentlemen from abroad dance with lustful intentions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives CA, short for circa; 'at first' places it ahead of the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballeros are Spanish gentlemen, so foreign from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: I have to deal with letter: shall we look? No time

definitions.text: I have to deal with letter

indicators.note: No here asks for the letter for time to be left out

parts.note: 'let's see' is a way of saying shall we look

explanation.surface: Someone told to deal with a letter suggests having a look, but there is no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' drops T (time) from LET'S SEE. The definition is a riddle: the 'letter' is one who lets out property, a landlord, whom a tenant must deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a lease from a landlord, the 'letter' who lets the property, so must deal with that person.

clue.text: Conference needed money everyone chipped in

indicators.note: chipped in suggests a contribution placed inside the word for money

parts.note: tin is British slang for money
each means every one

explanation.surface: A meeting went ahead because everybody contributed cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' for money is old British slang; 'chipped in' signals that one word goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal conference or series of lectures on one topic.

clue.text: Omission of written material appearing dotty?

definitions.text: Omission of written material appearing dotty?

parts.words: Omission of written material appearing dotty?
parts.note: words left out of a text are marked by a row of dots, so the gap looks dotty

explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsis is the omission of words, shown in print by three dots.

clue.text: Getting behind with job in the attic?

definitions.meaning: falling behind or trailing, as a slow walker does
the work of fitting insulation round tanks and pipes or across the loft floor

explanation.definitionFit: Lagging means falling behind, and lagging is also the insulating material fitted to lofts and pipes.

clue.text: Quite acceptable food topped with sticky stuff

indicators.note: topped with means the sticky word sits on top of the word for food in this down clue

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
a dish is a prepared food

explanation.surface: A tasty meal covered in a gooey sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped with' puts GOO above DISH in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodish means fairly good, so quite acceptable.

clue.text: Pest is left out, put in the shade

indicators.note: left out means the word is is removed from the word for pest

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: An annoying person is excluded and put in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes IS from NUISANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle difference, a shade of meaning.

clue.text: Channel crossing

definitions.meaning: a channel dug through ground for a road, railway or canal

explanation.definitionFit: A railway cutting is a dug channel, and cutting through a place means crossing it.

clue.text: Showing doubt like a philosopher

parts.note: as means like
Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher

explanation.surface: Sceptical, as a philosopher would be.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askant is to look sideways with suspicion or doubt.

clue.text: I read something on computer screen

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully

explanation.surface: Someone reads something on a monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: To con is an old word for studying a text closely.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a small picture on a computer display standing for a program or file.

clue.text: Having chosen people, is almost impetuous in retaining the best

indicators.note: retaining means holding the word for the best inside
almost means the last letter of the word for impetuous is cut

parts.note: rash means impetuous, acting without thought
the elite are the best of a group

explanation.surface: Being selected, someone is nearly reckless in keeping only top performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter of the word for impetuous; 'retaining' signals that it holds the best inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites are the biblical people described as God's chosen people.

clue.text: Birds ponder with tail lifted high

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for ponder is lifted to the top of this down entry

parts.note: to muse is to ponder

explanation.surface: Birds think things over with their tails cocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tail lifted high' moves the final E of MUSE to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds.

clue.text: One records a shocking experience, being out to mesmerise

indicators.note: being out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a startling experience, determined to mesmerise listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out' rearranges TO MESMERISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seismometer records earthquakes, which are literally shocks to the ground.

clue.text: One princess and another losing her head

indicators.note: losing her head means the first letter of the name is lost

parts.note: another princess: Aida, the Ethiopian princess of Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: Two princesses, one of whom is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; 'losing her head' drops the first A of AIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the title character of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera, so she is one princess.

clue.text: It may create second church with distinct set of beliefs

definitions.text: It may create second church with distinct set of beliefs

parts.note: an ism is a doctrine or system of belief

explanation.surface: A split may produce a breakaway church with its own creed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes what a split in a church does.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split in a church, which may produce a breakaway body holding its own doctrine.

clue.text: I locate sound and vision

indicators.note: sound means the words are said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: to site is to locate, so 'I locate' gives I SITE

explanation.surface: Someone claims to find their way by hearing and seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns I SITE (I locate) into its homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, which is vision.
